title: Build a choice-preserving support plan after a violation

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: Choice-preserving support responds to the person’s actual request and the service’s actual scope. Consent to one task does not authorize contact, touch, reporting or disclosure beyond it.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Fictional privacy breach: Ren wants a quiet text exchange, declines touch and retelling, and asks only for help finding the venue’s independent privacy-complaint route. The venue publishes an accessible written route to a privacy coordinator who was not involved. A general counseling service also exists but its eligibility and confidentiality details are unverified. No immediate danger or reporting duty is established by these facts.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Offer the requested help, identify which route matches it and preserve questions that need verification. Do not infer that one provider serves every kind of betrayal.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A recipient accepts help finding a service, then asks the helper not to send the prepared message. Does the earlier agreement authorize sending?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: The independent privacy route fits the requested procedural help; counseling may be an optional separate need after scope is checked. Later fiction: Ren saves the public route but chooses not to submit. No complaint or recovery occurred. Partial: locate help but imply a duty to use it. Incorrect: contact the person who breached privacy or promise absolute secrecy without knowing applicable limits.
criteria: Unknown service and confidentiality details stay unknown

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No. Respect the current choice within actual legal/safety duties; preserve the unsent draft and explain any genuine limit honestly rather than inventing one. Finding a route is not permission to disclose.
criteria: Unknown service and confidentiality details stay unknown
